experiment: E2/E3 lane x thermal + E2b substrate diagnostic
hypothesis: Faults crossing channels leave knickpoints whose strike alignment across independent drainages survives scarp degradation (Kirby & Whipple 2012; Perron & Royden 2013); thermal evidence (GDR 1391 springs/wells, 2 m probes, paleo sinter/travertine) should concentrate the same structures, adding off-catalogue recall to the lane.
mechanism: Priority-Flood fill -> D8 accumulation -> chi/ksn (theta = 0.45) on the 3DEP-10m-reduced 100 m pack -> knickpoint detection -> strike-concordance gating across >=3 independent first-order drainages -> thermal splat (max-splat, sigma = 3 px, normalised by the 99.9th percentile) -> 2-px catalogue ring -> 3-px NMS -> budgeted emission.
named_confound: A lithologic resistance contrast along a range front produces the same strike-aligned steepness steps. The substrate diagnostic adds a second, measured confound: on 100 m elevation the extracted channel network is itself partly an artefact of sampling and depression filling (Hack exponent b = +0.0264 / -0.0272 against 1.6-2.0 for real networks; the two independent 100 m products' channel networks agree at Jaccard 0.2312).

instrument_selection.truth: SGMC off-catalogue, thinned to 8,000 px, seed 61

uniqueness.note: gate is on rank correlation; Pearson on the union support is reported as the conservative companion since both rasters are binary

substrate_diagnostic.citation: Hack (1957) USGS Prof. Paper 294-B; Rigon et al. (1996) Water Resources Research 32, 3189-3194 (b ~ 1.6-2.0 for real networks)
substrate_diagnostic.verdict: Both 100 m products fail published drainage-network validity tests, so the lane's negative verdict is a RESOLUTION verdict. Fix = free 3DEP 10 m (or 1 m) elevation, fetchable on the GitHub Actions runner, not a new detector.

verdict: NEGATIVE - do not spend a submission slot. Loses to every control on the pooled hide-and-recover instrument and sits ~76x below the family's hard slot gate (best promotable holdout DTI 0.190147).
